title: Order Credits on Identification Corrections — Insurance Coverage & Claims Training Questions
content:
**Training questions — Insurance Coverage & Claims, identification corrections (CO-31).** These answers set out when credits on the patient's order under **Laboratory Test Orders** come off the base of an identification correction. The order is the order the corrected claim bills; its credits are the test charge credits on it, each carrying a credit reason.

**When do the order's credits enter an identification correction at all?**
Only when the order's most recent credit was posted after the claim's filing date, that is, on a later calendar day than the filing date. Where the most recent credit is dated on or before the filing date, or the order has no credit, nothing comes off.

**Which credits come off when they do enter?**
- Where any credit on the order is for a test not performed or a duplicate test, every credit on the order comes off.
- Where the order carries billing-correction credits only and their total reaches the identification correction's credit minimum, the billing-correction credits come off.
- Otherwise nothing comes off.

**What happens to the credits that come off?**
They are taken off the base.

**Worked question (hypothetical order).** The most recent credit is dated after the filing date; the order carries a duplicate-test credit of 35.00 USD and a billing-correction credit of 4.00 USD. A duplicate-test credit is present, so every credit comes off: 39.00 USD. Had the order carried only the billing-correction credit of 4.00 USD, it would come off only if 4.00 reached the credit minimum.

**Does a billing-correction credit total equal to the credit minimum count?** Yes; "reaches" includes equality.
